title: Microcontroller device-family register specification
description: Vendor-agnostic schema for microcontroller device-family register-map and peripheral register/field metadata.

spec-version.description: Spec format version using semantic versioning (semver), e.g. '1.0.0'. Increment the patch version for corrections, the minor version for backward-compatible additions, and the major version for breaking changes.

sub-families.description: List of sub-family identifiers that belong to this family.

arch-ref.description: Identifier of the architecture-level spec file (without the .yml extension) in docs/specs/common/arch/, e.g. 'cortex-m0plus'. Tooling can merge the referenced architecture spec with this family spec when generating code or documentation.

title.description: Human-readable title of the reference manual, e.g. 'STM32U0 series advanced Arm-based 32-bit MCUs - Reference Manual'.

revision.description: Reference manual revision identifier. Numeric for vendors that use integer revisions (e.g. 4); a quoted string for vendors that use letter or alphanumeric codes (e.g. 'I', 'B.1').

last-modified.description: Year-month when this revision of the reference manual was last modified, in YYYY-MM format (e.g. '2025-07').

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for the memory map as a whole.

definitions.description: Reusable definitions. Values are referenced via YAML anchors/aliases in the spec.

settings.description: Named settings maps, each referenced by one or more fields.

peripherals.description: List of peripheral blocks documented in this spec.

features.description: Per-sub-family feature/peripheral availability table extracted from the reference manual.

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for the features table as a whole.

data.description: Feature availability map. Keys are feature or peripheral names (e.g. 'AES', 'USB'). Values are mappings from sub-family identifier (e.g. 'stm32u031') to a boolean indicating whether that feature is present in that sub-family.

nvic.description: Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller configuration and vector table.

exti.description: Extended Interrupt and Event Controller line connections.

gpio-exti.description: GPIO external interrupt and wake-up line capability metadata.

boot.description: Boot-mode configuration table (e.g. Table 6 in RM0503). Lists the available boot modes and the pin states that select them.

low-power-modes.description: Low-power mode summary table for the device family (e.g. Table 21 in RM0503 §4.3). Each entry describes one low-power mode with its entry conditions, wake-up sources, clock behaviour, and voltage regulator states.

peripheral-mode-availability.description: Per-peripheral availability cross-reference for each working mode (e.g. Table 22 in RM0503 §4.3). Each entry lists a peripheral or component with its availability (Y/O/-) and wake-up capability in each working mode.

hex-address.description: A hex address or byte offset (e.g. 0x40000000). Written in hex notation in the source YAML; parsed as an integer by most YAML parsers.

references.description: Cross-references into the source reference manual.

section.description: Single section reference (used by individual registers).

memory-region.description: A named address range in the memory map.

base.description: Peripheral base address for register offset calculations, when it differs from the region's start address. Consumers must use this address (not start) when computing register addresses from offsets.

verified.description: Whether this entry has been verified against the reference manual. Defaults to true. Set to false to flag data that is provisional or still needs checking.

settings.description: Enumerated bit-pattern settings for a field. Keys are binary bit patterns (e.g. '00', '10', '1111'). Null means no settings are documented.

field.description: A named bit-field within a register.

name.description: Field name as it appears in the reference manual.

width.description: Field width in bits (must equal msb - lsb + 1).

access.description: Register field access type, using RM0503 §1.2 abbreviations exactly: rw = read/write; r = read-only; w = write-only; rc_w0 = read/clear by writing 0; rc_w1 = read/clear by writing 1; rc_w = read/clear by any write; rc_r = read/clear by reading; rs_r = read/set by reading; rs = read/set by software; rwo = read/write once after reset; t = toggle by writing 1; rt_w1 = read, writing 1 triggers an event (no effect on bit value); res = reserved (must not be modified by software).

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for this field.

priority-over.description: Names of fields that this field overrides when both are written in the same register access. If this field and any listed field are both written with a non-zero value simultaneously, the effect of this field takes precedence and the listed fields' writes are ignored by the hardware.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of when/why this sequence is required, and any caller arguments it accepts (e.g. 'write-arg' values).

steps.description: Ordered list of steps. Steps must be executed in the order listed.

sequence-step.description: A single step in a register access sequence.

op.description: Operation type: 'write' writes field values to the register; 'read' reads the register.

note.description: Human-readable explanation of this step's purpose, including any timing or ordering constraints.

optional.description: Whether this step may be omitted. Defaults to false. Optional steps should still be executed when possible.

fields.description: Field values to write. Keys are field names (or logical field groups). Values are either a non-negative integer literal (fixed value) or the string 'write-arg' (caller-supplied value). Only valid when op is 'write'.

expect.description: Expected field values to verify after reading. Keys are field names; values are the expected non-negative integers representing the field's bit pattern. A consumer should check these values and treat a mismatch as a sequence failure. Omit on read steps where the result is intentionally discarded. Only valid when op is 'read'.

offset.description: Register byte offset from the peripheral base address.

reset-value.description: Register value after reset, as documented in the reference manual.

source-table.description: Reference manual table number or identifier that documents the field layout of this register.

sub-families.description: Sub-families for which this register is present. Omit if the register is present in all sub-families.

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for this register, e.g. to document cross-register dependencies or constraints not expressible in the structured fields.

fields.description: Ordered list of bit-fields from MSB to LSB.

peripheral-feature-profile.description: Structured feature profile for a peripheral family tier (for example 'full', 'basic', or 'low-power').

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for this feature profile.

includes.description: Features that are supported by this profile.

excludes.description: Features that are explicitly not supported by this profile.

peripheral-feature-set-value.description: Feature value for a feature set column. Uses booleans for supported/unsupported features, strings for descriptive/noted values, and integers for numeric quantities (for example FIFO size in bytes).

peripheral-feature-set-row.description: A single feature row from a peripheral feature-set table.

note.description: Optional annotation for this feature row (for example reference-manual notes such as 'note 2').

peripheral-feature-sets.description: Structured feature-set table metadata and rows for peripherals that define Full/Basic/Low-power tiers (for example STM32 USART/LPUART feature tables).

source.description: Source identifier of the feature-set table, e.g. 'Table 200'.

section.description: Reference-manual section where the feature-set table is documented, e.g. '34.4'.

page.description: Reference-manual page number where the feature-set table appears.

features.description: Ordered feature rows from the feature-set table.

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for this peripheral, e.g. to document the port-pair mapping or address layout conventions.

feature-profiles.description: Optional named feature profiles shared by instances of this peripheral. Instances can reference one of these names via peripheral-instance.feature-profile.

feature-sets.description: Optional structured feature-set table data for this peripheral.

instances.description: Concrete instances of this peripheral in the device memory map, each binding the register layout to a named base address.

registers.description: Ordered list of register definitions. Each item is a single-key mapping whose key is the register name.

register-map.description: Ordered register-map table for this peripheral, listing every register with its offset and reset value. Serves as the authoritative source for verifying individual register definitions.

interrupt-events.description: Structured interrupt event metadata for this peripheral, including per-event flag/enable/clear information and low-power mode behaviour.

clock-sources.description: Optional list of clock sources that can drive this peripheral, as documented in the clock-controller chapter of the reference manual.

dma-requests.description: Optional list of DMA request lines that this peripheral can issue, as documented in the DMAMUX assignment table of the reference manual.

flash-wait-states.description: Flash wait-state table for this peripheral (applicable only to flash memory controllers). Derived from the reference manual wait-state table (e.g. Table 9 in RM0503 §3.3.3).

clock-source-freq-table.description: Clock source maximum frequency table by voltage range for this peripheral (applicable to clock-controller peripherals, e.g. Table 32 in RM0503 §5.2.9).

register-map-entry.description: A single entry in a peripheral register-map table, recording the register name, byte offset, reset value, and optional source-table reference.

name.description: Register name as it appears in the reference manual.

offset.description: Register byte offset from the peripheral base address.

reset-value.description: Register value after reset, as documented in the reference manual.

source-table.description: Reference manual table number or identifier that is the source for this register-map entry.

peripheral-instance.description: A named instance of a peripheral at a specific base address.

name.description: Instance name as it appears in the reference manual, e.g. 'GPIOA', 'TIM2'.

base.description: Base address of this peripheral instance.

sub-families.description: Sub-families for which this instance is present. Omit if the instance is present in all sub-families.

feature-profile.description: Name of the feature profile from peripheral.feature-profiles that applies to this instance.

feature-set.description: Feature-set tier for this instance (for example 'full-feature-set', 'basic-feature-set', or 'low-power-feature-set').

alternate-functions.description: GPIO alternate-function pin mappings for this peripheral instance. Each entry names a GPIO pin, the AF number (0-15) used to select this peripheral on that pin, and the signal routed when that AF is active. Source: device datasheet alternate-function tables (e.g. Table 16 in DS14463), not RM0503.

register-item.description: A single-key mapping where the key is the register name and the value is the register definition.

peripheral-item.description: A single-key mapping where the key is the peripheral name and the value is the peripheral definition.

clock-source-item.description: A single clock source that can drive a peripheral, as documented in the clock-controller chapter of the reference manual.

bus.description: Bus or clock domain this source belongs to, e.g. 'APB1', 'APB2', 'AHB'.

enable-bit.description: Name of the clock-gating bit that enables this clock source for the peripheral, e.g. 'USART1EN', 'TIM2EN'.

dma-request-item.description: A single DMA request line that a peripheral can issue, as documented in the DMAMUX assignment table of the reference manual.

request-name.description: Name of the DMA request signal as it appears in the reference manual, e.g. 'USART1_RX', 'TIM2_UP'.

channel-id.description: DMA channel identifier associated with this request, if statically assigned. May be an integer channel number or a string label.

mux-input.description: DMAMUX input number assigned to this request, as listed in the DMAMUX assignment table (e.g. Table 49 in RM0503).

peripheral-interrupt-events.description: Structured interrupt event metadata for a peripheral, extracted from the reference manual interrupt-request table.

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for the interrupt event table.

interrupt-event.description: A single interrupt event with its status flag, enable bit, clear method, and low-power mode exit behaviour.

event.description: Human-readable name of the interrupt event.

flag.description: Status flag name in the ISR register.

enable-bit.description: Interrupt enable bit or bit-group name in the control register.

clear-method.description: How to clear the interrupt flag.

exit-sleep.description: Whether this interrupt can wake the MCU from Sleep mode.

exit-stop.description: Whether this interrupt can wake the MCU from Stop mode.

exit-standby.description: Whether this interrupt can wake the MCU from Standby mode.

notes.description: Optional free-text annotation for this interrupt event.

interrupt-low-power-modes.description: Describes peripheral interrupt behaviour in each low-power mode.

nvic.description: Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller configuration and vector table.

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for the NVIC.

priority-bits.description: Number of priority bits implemented in hardware.

systick-calibration.description: SysTick TENMS calibration value: the number of SysTick ticks for 10 ms at the SysTick reference clock frequency.

system-exceptions.description: Cortex-M system exceptions (non-maskable and fixed-priority entries).

vectors.description: Peripheral (maskable) interrupt vectors ordered by IRQ position number.

acronym.description: System exception acronym/stem from the vector table (e.g. 'Reset', 'HardFault').

priority.description: Exception priority value. Negative for fixed-priority exceptions (e.g. -3 = Reset); non-negative for settable ones.

priority-type.description: Whether the priority is fixed by hardware or configurable in software.

address.description: Vector table address of this exception.

position.description: IRQ number — 0-based position in the vector table after the system exceptions.

acronym.description: IRQ acronym/stem from the vector table (e.g. 'WWDG_IWDG'). The startup handler symbol is typically this value with '_IRQHandler' appended.

description.description: Human-readable description of what triggers this interrupt.

exti-lines.description: EXTI line numbers that are combined into this interrupt vector, if any.

sub-families.description: Sub-families for which this vector entry is valid. Omit if valid on all sub-families. Use multiple entries with the same position to represent sub-family-specific variants.

address.description: Vector table address of this interrupt.

exti.description: Extended Interrupt and Event Controller line connection table.

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for the EXTI line table.

lines.description: EXTI line definitions ordered by line number.

exti-line.description: A single EXTI line connection entry.

source.description: Peripheral or signal connected to this EXTI line.

type.description: Configurable lines have EXTI pending bits cleared by writing 1 to EXTI_RPR1/EXTI_FPR1. Direct lines have no EXTI pending bit and are cleared in the peripheral.

notes.description: Optional free-text annotation for this EXTI line.

reserved-on.description: Sub-family identifiers (e.g. 'stm32u031') on which this EXTI line is reserved and not implemented.

gpio-exti.description: GPIO external interrupt and wake-up capability metadata.

exti-lines.description: EXTI line range used for GPIO interrupts, expressed as an inclusive range string (e.g. '0-15').

supported-ports.description: GPIO port identifiers that support external interrupt via EXTI (e.g. 'PA', 'PB').

pin-modes-allowed.description: GPIO modes in which external interrupt capability is supported.

pin-modes-forbidden.description: GPIO modes in which external interrupt capability is not supported.

boot.description: Boot-mode configuration block. Captures the boot-mode selection table from the reference manual (e.g. RM0503 Table 6).

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for the boot-mode table as a whole.

modes.description: List of boot modes supported by the device family.

boot-mode.description: A single entry in the boot-mode selection table.

name.description: Short semantic identifier for this boot mode, e.g. 'main-flash', 'system-memory', 'sram', 'main-flash-forced'.

boot-pin-state.description: Required state of the BOOT pin (or equivalent signal) to select this mode, e.g. '0', '1', or a free-text description. Use 'conditions' instead when multiple configuration inputs govern mode selection.

conditions.description: Map of configuration-input names to their required values for this boot mode. Keys are the exact signal or bit names from the reference manual (e.g. 'BOOT_LOCK', 'nBOOT_SEL', 'BOOT0_pin', 'nBOOT1', 'nBOOT0'). Values are '0', '1', or 'x' (don't care).

source.description: Human-readable description of the boot memory source for this mode, e.g. 'Main Flash memory', 'System memory (bootloader)', 'Embedded SRAM'.

af-mapping.description: A single GPIO alternate-function mapping: the GPIO pin, AF number, and the peripheral signal activated when that AF is selected.

pin.description: GPIO pin identifier in the form 'PA8', 'PB3', etc.

af-number.description: Alternate-function selection number (0-15) written to the GPIO AFRL/AFRH register to route the signal to this pin.

signal.description: Peripheral signal name activated on this pin when the AF is selected, e.g. 'TIM1_CH1', 'USART2_TX'.

sub-families.description: Sub-families for which this mapping is valid. Omit if valid on all sub-families.

flash-wait-states.description: Flash memory wait-state table by voltage range (e.g. Table 9 in RM0503 §3.3.3). Defines the maximum HCLK frequency for each combination of wait-state count and voltage range.

entries.description: List of wait-state rows, one per wait-state count, in ascending order.

flash-wait-state-entry.description: A single row from the flash wait-state table: the wait-state count (LATENCY value) and the maximum HCLK frequency in MHz for each voltage range.

ws.description: Wait-state count, equal to the LATENCY field value written to FLASH_ACR.

cpu-cycles.description: Number of CPU cycles per flash read access (equal to ws + 1).

max-hclk-mhz.description: Map from voltage-range name to the maximum HCLK frequency in MHz for that range at this wait-state count. Keys are the exact voltage-range names from the reference manual table (e.g. 'V Range 1 CORE', 'V Range 2 CORE').

clock-source-freq-table.description: Maximum clock-source frequency table by voltage range (e.g. Table 32 in RM0503 §5.2.9). Defines the maximum frequency in MHz for each named clock source at each voltage range.

notes.description: Optional footnotes or annotations for the table as a whole, in the order they appear in the reference manual.

entries.description: List of clock-source rows in the order given by the reference manual.

clock-source-freq-entry.description: A single row from the clock-source frequency table: the clock name and the maximum frequency in MHz for each voltage range.

name.description: Clock source name as given in the reference manual, e.g. 'HSI16', 'HSE', 'SYSCLK'.

note.description: Optional annotation for this entry, e.g. to document availability constraints.

max-freq-mhz.description: Map from voltage-range name to the maximum frequency in MHz for that range. Omit the key if the clock source is not available in that range.

low-power-mode-table.description: Container for the device-family low-power mode summary table (e.g. Table 21 in RM0503 §4.3).

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for the table as a whole.

modes.description: List of low-power mode entries, one per mode, in the order given by the reference manual.

low-power-mode-entry.description: A single entry in the low-power mode summary table.

name.description: Low-power mode name as given in the reference manual, e.g. 'Sleep', 'Stop 0', 'Standby'.

entry.description: Instruction(s) or condition(s) used to enter this mode.

wakeup-source.description: Events or signals that wake the device from this mode.

wakeup-clock.description: System clock active immediately after wake-up from this mode.

effect-on-clocks.description: Effect on clock sources while the device is in this mode.

main-regulator.description: State of the main voltage regulator (MR) in this mode.

lp-regulator.description: State of the low-power voltage regulator (LPR) in this mode.

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for this mode entry.

peripheral-mode-availability-table.description: Container for the per-peripheral working-mode availability table (e.g. Table 22 in RM0503 §4.3).

note.description: Optional free-text annotation for the table as a whole.

footnotes.description: Numbered footnotes referenced by cell values in the entries.

entries.description: List of peripheral availability entries, one per peripheral row, in the order given by the reference manual.

peripheral-mode-footnote.description: A numbered footnote for the peripheral mode availability table.

number.description: Footnote number as it appears in the reference manual table.

peripheral-mode-availability-entry.description: Availability of one peripheral or component in each working mode. Values are Y (always enabled), O (optional/software-enabled), - (not available), or a string combining these with a footnote reference such as 'O(1)' or '5 pins (10)'.

peripheral.description: Peripheral or component name as given in the reference manual table.
